messages:
kevin.s: Hey folks — ran out of my prescription (controlled med) while in Lisbon. Pharmacy says they can do an emergency refill only with insurer pre-auth or an "authorization letter" from employer. I paid cash. Can benefits issue something quick? I'm at the conference until tomorrow evening.

leo.benefits: Sorry you're dealing with that. For controlled substances, insurers are extra cautious. We can produce a proof-of-coverage + a short employer authorization letter stating the member is active and authorizing the pharmacy to contact claims for verification. Note: we cannot issue medical pre-auths or replace a doctors prescription. Did pharmacy ask for a reference number or just a signed letter?

kevin.s: They asked for either an insurer pre-auth code OR a company authorization letter with policy number and a contact that the pharmacy can call/email. They said without that they can only dispense a 3-day emergency supply.

claims_bot: Automated guidance: For international pharmacy claims, submit at https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Pharmacy / Prescription". Required: itemized receipt, prescription copy, attending physician name, currency, and proof of payment. Processing time 2-5 business days for pharmacy-specific claims. Emergency authorizations: contact claims@redwood.com or call +1-800-555-0199.

sophia.hr: We can also escalate as a medical-travel emergency if this blocks you from travel or work. Kevin, DM me your passport name & member ID and I'll flag it.

leo.benefits: Draft I can hand them (copy/paste or print):
```
Redwood Inference - Benefits Claims
Policy #: RW-PL-2039
Member: Kevin S. (Member ID: 0098876)
Claims intake: claims@redwood.com
International claims phone: +1-800-555-0199 (limited hours)

To whom it may concern,
This letter confirms the above-named is an active plan member. The employer authorizes the provider/pharmacy to contact the insurer for verification of coverage and to submit invoices for direct billing where permitted. This letter is for verification purposes only and is not a guarantee of payment.
```

isabel.pharmacy: Hi Kevin, from the pharmacy side: if you hand us that letter and a copy/photo of the prescription and ID, we can do a 3-day emergency dispense right away and email invoice to claims@redwood.com. For a full refill we need insurer confirmation. The pharmacy will attempt to call the claims number but sometimes emails work better for international insurers.

kevin.s: Thanks Isabel — that would help, 3 days is enough to get through tonight. Can People Ops include a Spanish/Portuguese line so staff understand?

leo.benefits: Sure. I'll add Portuguese: "Por favor, contacte claims@redwood.com para verificar cobertura." Also will include a short note: "For emergency 72-hour refill, pharmacy may dispense pending insurer confirmation."

sophia.hr: Kevin, send me the prescription photo and your member ID now. I'll ping claims and ask for an expedited verification call.

kevin.s: Uploaded the prescription and receipt to the portal and DM'd you the passport name. Pharmacy accepted the printed letter and gave me a 72-hour supply. Thanks team.

leo.benefits: Follow-up: after you return, submit the original prescription + itemized receipt to the portal for HSA eligibility / reimbursement if needed. If they email an invoice directly to claims@redwood.com, forward it to us and I'll mark the case urgent.

isabel.pharmacy: We emailed the invoice to claims@redwood.com with pharmacy VAT and bank details. Please tell them to look for subject "Invoice for Kevin S. - Emergency Rx".

kevin.s: Received the medication, feeling better. Appreciate the quick turnaround :relieved:
